questions.q: Why do introverts tend to dislike small talk, according to the summary?
a: They process stimuli more thoroughly and prefer deeper subjects
They are less curious about other people's lives
They find it harder to remember names and faces
They were taught to avoid talking to strangers
questions.why: Lesson 1 says introverts take in information deeply, so they are engaged by profound conversation.

questions.q: What does the summary say Western culture often confuses?
a: Confidence with competence
Kindness with weakness
Silence with sadness
Ambition with intelligence
questions.why: Lesson 2 says we tend to see the most confident person as the most competent one.

questions.q: Which achievement does the summary offer as an example of solitary work?
a: Einstein developing the theory of relativity
Steve Jobs pitching a new phone
Oprah hosting a daily talk show
Ford building a moving assembly line
questions.why: Lesson 3 notes that Einstein worked out relativity alone, as did the writer of Harry Potter.

questions.q: How does the summary describe most office environments for introverts?
a: Full of interruptions and information overload
Quiet and suited to deep concentration
Built around private rooms and closed doors
Designed mainly for people working remotely
questions.why: Lesson 3 says open offices, meetings and brainstorming leave introverts stressed and overloaded.

questions.q: What does the summary say Harvard tries to do with its graduates?
a: Groom them into extroverts through group work and seminars
Train them to work alone for long stretches
Discourage them from joining campus clubs
Select only students who prefer silence
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Harvard pushes students through group work, seminars and social events.
